CANONICAL HOST: Virginia Tech University Libraries (figshare-backed data.lib.vt.edu) -- NOT UT Austin Radionavigation Lab, ORNL, Zenodo, or IEEE DataPort. verified.name: TEXBAT (Texas Spoofing Test Battery, UT Austin Radionavigation Lab, raw IF)
verified.format: Raw IF / baseband samples. Binary .bin files of complex (I+Q) samples at 25 Msps, 16-bit per component (int16), i.e. 4 bytes/sample, ~7 min (420 s) per scenario. NOT processed correlator dumps and NOT RINEX. A MATLAB helper (scott.m) is provided to read the binary into MATLAB.
verified.approx_size: ~42 GB per scenario (420 s x 25e6 samples/s x 4 bytes/sample = ~42 GB); ~400 GB total for all ~9 files (cleanStatic + ds1-ds8). NOTE: per-file/total sizes are COMPUTED from the verified format (25 Msps, 16-bit complex, ~420 s) because the rnl-data directory index could not be reached from this environment to read exact byte counts; they are deterministic, not invented.
verified.download_method: Direct HTTP download, no login/EULA/registration. Browse the open Apache directory index at https://rnl-data.ae.utexas.edu/datastore/texbat/ and download each scenario file (cleanStatic.bin, ds1.bin ... ds8.bin) plus the MATLAB reader scott.m. Example: wget -r -np -nH --cut-dirs=2 -A '*.bin,*.m' https://rnl-data.ae.utexas.edu/datastore/texbat/ ; or per-file: wget https://rnl-data.ae.utexas.edu/datastore/texbat/ds2.bin . The main landing page (https://radionavlab.ae.utexas.edu/texbat/) links to this datastore via 'download directly from UT'. If download fails, contact todd.humphreys@utexas.edu. CAVEAT: from this sandbox the rnl-data.ae.utexas.edu host reset the connection (curl error 35 / WebFetch socket close) on every attempt, so an automated agent may hit host-side throttling/geofencing or TLS issues; the radionavlab.ae.utexas.edu landing page was reachable.
observables: raw IF / baseband complex IQ samples (25 Msps, 16-bit int16 I+Q)
GPS L1 C/A (live-sky authentic + spoofed signal combined in recording)
verified.notes: VERIFIED via multiple reachable canonical/secondary sources: (1) Official landing page https://radionavlab.ae.utexas.edu/texbat/ (FETCHED) confirms datasets are 'download directly from UT' at /datastore/texbat/, lists cleanStatic + ds1-ds6 (TEXBAT 1.0) plus ds7.bin/ds8.bin added Aug 2015 (TEXBAT 1.1), provides MATLAB helper scott.m (Logan Scott), no login/EULA, contact todd.humphreys@utexas.edu. (2) wasyresearch public-datasets page (FETCHED) confirms '25 MHz with 16-bit quantisation', I/Q raw IF samples, 8 spoofing scenarios. (3) GitHub gist (FETCHED) confirms 'all eight TEXBAT spoofing scenario signals contain base band complex samples at a rate of 25MSPS' with 'approximately 7 minutes (420 seconds)' per file. (4) Lemmenes 'Detailed Analysis of the TEXBAT Datasets' paper (FETCHED + pdftotext extracted) confirms a GRADED POWER SWEEP across scenarios: Scenario 2 ~10 dB power advantage, Scenario 3 1.3 dB, Scenario 4 0.4 dB (so datasets provide graded spoofer-to-authentic power / quasi-J:S impairment levels); it also shows correlator E/P/L taps are PRODUCED BY A SOFTWARE RECEIVER (GEARS, 61 taps) from the raw samples -> TEXBAT itself ships ONLY raw IF, no processed correlator taps. Scenario taxonomy: cleanStatic (authentic), ds1 abrupt/switched takeover (static), ds2 time-push overpowered (~10 dB), ds3 time-push matched-power (1.3 dB), ds4 position-push matched-power (0.4 dB), ds5/ds6 dynamic time-push/position-push, ds7 carrier-phase-aligned matched-power time-push, ds8 zero-delay SCER replay variant of ds7 (per landing page + ds7/ds8 white paper title). FEASIBILITY = HEAVY: each .bin is ~42 GB (tens of GB raw IF) and the full battery is ~400 GB, far beyond a <2GB laptop direct-download threshold; an agent would need to selectively pull 1-2 scenarios (~42 GB each) and run its own SDR tracking to derive correlator/SQM features. ACCESS is technically open (no paywall/login) but the rnl-data host was NOT reachable from this sandbox (connection reset on every curl/WebFetch attempt) -> automated retrieval may be blocked by host throttling/geofence; verify reachability before relying on it. No DOI; not on Zenodo/IEEE DataPort (UT Austin self-hosted). Related/complementary: OAKBAT (Oak Ridge Spoofing and Interference Test Battery, ORNL, OSTI) and TEXCUP also from this lab.

CLI alternative: `globus transfer 57618e0a-2c99-45ff-9694-24141b92fa17:/gen101/world-shared/doi-data/ORNLNCCS/202009/10.13139_ORNLNCCS_1664429/ <your-endpoint>:<dest> --recursive` (requires `globus login`). No paywall/EULA, but a Globus identity (e.g. ORCID/Google/institutional login) is required - so it is NOT a plain unauthenticated wget.
verified.notes:
VERIFIED by fetching the ORNL Constellation DOI page (Globus origin ID + path confirmed), the OSTI/DOE Data Explorer catalog (DOIs + binary-RF description confirmed), and by reading the full ION GNSS+ 2020 conference paper PDF directly (Albright, Powers, Bonior, Combs - OSTI 1836467) which gives the authoritative specs.

NAME CORRECTION: The dataset is "Oak Ridge Spoofing and INTERFERENCE Test Battery", not "Spoofing and Anomaly Battery". HOST CORRECTION: it is hosted by ORNL (Oak Ridge), NOT the UT Austin Radionavigation Lab - UT Austin RNL hosts TEXBAT, the dataset OAKBAT is a deliberate "sibling"/twin of. Do not cite UT Austin or Zenodo or IEEE DataPort for OAKBAT.

CONTENTS (16 datasets total): GPS L1 C/A = 2 clean baselines + 6 spoofing (os1a..os6); Galileo E1 = 2 clean baselines + 6 spoofing (identical params except constellation); plus a separate Pure Tones subset. All recordings start 2020-03-19 09:59:42 UTC, ~8 min static / ~8-10 min dynamic each.

GRADED SEVERITY (confirmed, mirrors TEXBAT ds2-ds5): os1a = static RF switch (600 m position offset); os2 = static time push at 10 dB spoofing power advantage; os3 = static time push at 1.3 dB advantage; os4 = static 600 m position push at 0.4 dB advantage; os5 = dynamic time push at 9.9 dB advantage; os6 (dynamic) completes the six. GPS sky power -125 dBm, spoof -125.4 to -115 dBm depending on scenario. This IS a graded power-advantage / effective-JSR sweep.

NO PROCESSED CORRELATOR TAPS: ships raw IF only. To get E/P/L correlator taps / SQM metrics you must run your own SDR/correlator (e.g. GNSS-SDR, FGI-GSRx, or your own tracking loop) over the IQ - exactly the SDR-tracking stage you are building in task #147. Adapting TEXBAT code only requires changing the 5 MHz sample rate (format is otherwise identical to TEXBAT).

FEASIBILITY = HEAVY for an automated laptop agent: total ~150-190 GB raw IF (estimate; ~75-95 GB GPS-only), and access is gated behind a Globus account (not a one-line wget). A single ~10 GB scenario is tractable on a laptop, but the full battery is tens-to-~hundreds of GB and the Globus auth step blocks fully unattended download. NOT "easy" (>2 GB and login-gated transfer agent), NOT "infeasible" (free account, open access, no paywall/EULA). Recommend pulling 1-2 graded GPS scenarios (e.g. os2 @10 dB + os3 @1.3 dB) for a graded-severity probe rather than the whole battery.

Reproducibility metadata + full RF file listing: https://github.com/oakbat (org repo). As of 2025 some secondary sources note OAKBAT access "requires some registration" - consistent with the Globus account requirement verified here.
